READING Time: 35 minutes (28 points) Mustangs The image of horses running freely across the plains is a popular symbol of the American West. However, mustangs are not native to the United States. When Spanish armies came to the New World in the sixteenth century, they brought horses with them. Horses had been extinct in the Americas for about 12,000 years. The wild horses that now live in the western part of the United States are called mustangs. The word comes from the Spanish word mesteño, meaning wild or stray. The mustangs’ ancestors were Spanish horses that had escaped from Spanish soldiers. (1) Over many years, the mustang population in the western United States grew. (2) By the end of the nineteenth century, about two million mustangs roamed the countryside. (3) Farmers and ranchers complained that the mustangs destroyed their crops and ate food meant for farm animals. (4) Some mustangs were used in movies about the Wild West. (5) Although some people tried to protect wild horses as early as 1925, the mustang population kept shrinking because many farmers killed them or removed them from the western plains and prairies. (6) By 1970, fewer than 17,000 mustangs remained in the USA. In 1971, the US Congress passed a law to protect these wild horses. Today, the government manages areas with too many mustangs. Some of the horses are even offered for adoption. About 37,000 mustangs currently live in the United States. 1. Guess the meanings of the following words. Match the words with their definitions. Together with their father they are visiting different European countries, including Russia. While in Moscow, they visited several museums. Listen to the dialogue between Laura, Frank and their father in one of the Moscow museums and answer the following questions. You will hear the dialogue twice. Now we are ready to start. Frank: Ah! Look! It’s a statue of David! Father: That’s right, Frank! It’s Michelangelo’s David! Frank: And in that other room I saw his Moses! We’ve just seen them in Florence! How come they are in Moscow? Laura: It’s because they are not real. Frank: What do you mean they are not real? They are the same size and they look exactly the same. Laura: Yes, but the real ones are in Italy. Michelangelo lived in Italy, remember? Tell him, Daddy! Father: Laura is right, Frank! These are copies. But you were the first to recognize these statues – real or not! I’m so proud of you! Frank: See? Laura: Show-off! Father: Hey, kids, I think it is now time to see the main reason I wanted to visit Moscow! It is in that room over there! Frank: Is it the Egyptian room? I want to see the mummies! Laura: Haven’t you just seen enough of them in the Louvre in Paris? And in London, in the British Museum? Frank: I wouldn’t mind seeing some more! Father: No, it is not the Egyptian room, Frank. It is the room of the Gold of Troy. It is the story of how a boy’s childhood dream came true. Laura: Wait a second, Daddy. When you say the Gold of Troy, you mean the legend, right? The myth of the ancient Greek city of Troy? The Trojan War, the Trojan Horse, soldiers hidden inside that wooden horse? That wasn’t real – was it? Father: Well, Laura, nobody knows if the Trojan War or the horse were real. But the city itself is a different story. For two thousand years people thought the city was also a legend and wasn’t real. But… in the 19th century, there was this German boy, and

his name was Heinrich Schliemann. When he was 7 years old, he decided that he would find the real ancient city of Troy. He loved the legend of Troy so much that he learnt the Greek language and when he grew up and made enough money, he went to Turkey and found it! Frank: Wow! Did he become an archaeologist? Father: That’s the thing! Officially, he didn’t! He couldn’t afford to go to university when he was young. But he kept reading about Troy. And when the right time came, he organized an archaeological expedition and found it – and proved to the whole world two things – that the legendary city of Troy really existed, but most importantly, that a childhood dream can come true. Laura: That’s so cool! Let’s go see what he found! Frank: And after that – the Egyptian room! Father: Deal! You’ll hear the dialogue again in 30 seconds.
